head: a458b3f5
gate: QUIC recovery queue caches per-payload STREAM/RESET_STREAM references instead of re-parsing every pending frame on each stream-credit query
problem: quic.recovery.Queue.hasPendingStreamFrame scanned every pending payload and re-decoded every frame on each call. peerStreamCreditState -> flushRequestedStreamReleasesAt -> requestCompletedPeerStreamRelease calls it per completed stream, so HTTP/3 multiplexing cost grew quadratically with concurrent streams. perf at 32 streams attributed 19.6% of samples to quic.parseFrameAfterType reached only from that scan.
change: PendingDatagram caches up to four parsed StreamRef entries inline; the first query parses the payload once and later queries only compare ids. Payload compaction in abandonStreamData invalidates the cache. Payloads with more than four stream references, undecodable frames, or a zero-length parse step fall back to the previous conservative 'has pending' answer.

benchmark.workload: weft bench-h3, synthetic handshake, one loopback connection, GET / -> 200 "ok"

http3.note: one run reported the known flaky CONNECT DATAGRAM pacing feedback test

notes: 32-stream GET improved 151.2 -> 65.3 us/request (2.3x) and upload 180.6 -> 91.8 us/request (2.0x). The per-request gap between 32 and 8 streams fell from 3.4x to 1.36x. The netz-only split shows both halves were affected: sending 32 requests dropped 845 -> 284 us per batch and receiving 32 responses 3802 -> 1286 us. Earlier rejected attempts (worker-pool caps, pacing ceiling, burst drain ahead of the command queue, bounded command-drain slices) are recorded in 2026-11-04-h3-burst-drain-rejected.json.
